# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet. I need the manual’s exact rule from the Mute, and the Deaf should report every visible marking, colour, and display/light state to the Mute so it can be relayed to me. I will not act until those independent pieces agree.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the manual's exact rule on your next turn. Also have the Deaf report the display, light, and all three wire colours and markings to you, then relay that complete visual report to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, light purple, and wires in order 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured five ? signs followed by three ? signs; I do not know their meaning.

I know the tactilely inaccessible facts only through the Deaf: display 0, purple light, and wire colours yellow, red, green. The Mute’s gestures have reached the Deaf, but their symbols are not identified here, so they cannot yet convey the manual’s rule reliably. I need the Deaf to describe those gestures and relay the manual’s instruction in words. I will not cut a wire based only on the colours.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please repeat the manual's complete rule using a clear, agreed sequence of gestures, and have the Deaf describe each gesture and its order to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 2: display 0; light is now yellow; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured five ?, then ?, then three ?. Your gesture ? was visible to me.

The Deaf’s report confirms the current state is display 0, yellow light, with wires yellow, red, green. The Mute’s gesture sequence still has no usable meaning to me. I will establish a simple output code: the Mute should signal the required wire by repeating one identical, unmistakable gesture once, twice, or three times. The Deaf can then report the count, which directly gives the wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: display 0; light yellow; wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. Use the manual to determine the required wire. Then gesture one identical sign for wire 1, two identical signs for wire 2, or three identical signs for wire 3. Do not add any other signs.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 3: display 0; light is red; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute repeated five ?, then ?, then three ?. Your new gesture was ?.

The current tactilely inaccessible state is now display 0, red light, and wires yellow/red/green. The Mute’s gestures are still not being relayed with their identities, so the sequence cannot safely be interpreted. I need the Mute to use only named gestures and the Deaf to report those names and their exact order; no wire should be cut until that relay is clear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use only these gestures, exactly as needed: 👍, 👎, 👌. Have the Deaf report the exact symbol names and counts to me. First convey the manual's complete rule, then convey the chosen wire position. Do not use any other gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 4: display 0; light is green; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I saw your gestures ? followed by ?.

The bomb’s visible state has changed again to display 0, green light, and wire colours yellow, red, green. I still do not know what the Mute’s five-one-three gesture sequence means; as the Blind, gesture symbols arrive to me only as blanks. The safe next step is for the Mute to direct the Deaf to describe the gestures in ordinary words, including any shape or orientation, and for the Deaf to report that description to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I receive your gestures only as blanks. Please gesture the manual rule to the Deaf, and instruct the Deaf to describe each sign aloud in ordinary words, including its hand shape and direction, followed by the required wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 5: display 0; light is white; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute now gestured ? ?. Your prior gestures received were ?, then ?, then ?, then ? ?.

The state is now display 0, white light, with wires still yellow, red, green. I still have no reliable interpretation of the Mute’s manual-derived signs, so cutting now would be unsafe. The Mute can nevertheless communicate the answer without exposing the manual: encode the selected wire as one, two, or three repetitions of a single identical gesture, and the Deaf must report only that count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Determine the correct wire from the manual and current state. Then make exactly one identical gesture for wire 1, exactly two repetitions for wire 2, or exactly three repetitions for wire 3. Make no other gestures. Deaf, report the repetition count plainly to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 6: display 0; light is orange; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again gestured ? ?.

The current state is display 0, orange light, and wires yellow, red, green. The Mute’s signs still do not provide me with an identifiable wire, and an action would be a guess. I will keep the bomb untouched and request a minimal, unambiguous relay: one, two, or three identical signs only, with the Deaf reporting the count.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send the five-sign/three-sign rule sequence. Send only the selected wire: one identical gesture means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Deaf, report the exact number of repeated signs.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 7: display 0; light is blue; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No new gesture arrived.

The latest state is display 0, blue light, with the same wire order. No answer from the Mute has been conveyed in a usable form, so cutting any wire remains unsafe. I will request the wire position once more using the simplest possible count-only protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="On your next turn, send only the answer as repeated identical gestures: one gesture for wire 1, two for wire 2, or three for wire 3. No rule explanation and no other gestures. Deaf, report only the count.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Turn 8: display 0; light is purple; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured ?.

The latest report contains exactly one gesture from the Mute. Under the count-only protocol we established, one repeated gesture means wire 1. The current bomb state last reported is display 0, purple light, with wires yellow, red, green. I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
